In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of novel compounds active against parasites of veterinary importance, such as the cat flea and Haemonchus.
the development of novel compounds that can act as anthelmintic agents against gastrointestinal and ectoparasitic nematodes and ectoparasites, respectively.
the synthesis and evaluation of novel 2-pheny-3-(1h-pyrrol- 2-yl) acrylonitrile analogs for their activity against the endo- and ectoparasites Haemonchuscontortus and C. felis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the compounds tested were not effective against H. contortus or C. felis in vitro.
the compounds 4b, 4e, 4f, 4g, 4i, 5b, and 5e showed significant activity against both H. contortus and cat flea.
the 2-phenylethynyl-3-(pyrrol-2-ylethynyl)acrylo derivatives were more active than the 2-aryl-3-(pyrol-2-ynyl)acrylic acid amides against H. contortus and against C. felis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have synthesized a series of (Z)-3-(1H-Pyrrol-2yl)acrylo derivatives, and we have found a series of compounds with activity against Haemonchous contortus.

the most active compound, 3-(1H-Pyrrol-2yl)acrylo nitrile, was found to have the highest activity with a 50% effective dose (ED50) value of 0.0001 μg/mL against H. contortus and 0.0003 μg/mL against C. felis.
the compounds with an unsubstituted phenyl group at the 2-position of the acrylonitrile moiety were more potent than those with a 4-methoxyphenyl group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 2-phenylethyl group is important for activity against the endo- and ectoparasites.

the presence of a 4-methoxy substituent at the 5-position of the pyrrole ring and an ethyl ester at the 3-position of the pyridine ring were the most important structural features for the activity of the synthesized compounds.
the presence of a halogen substituent at C4 of the pyrrol ring is important for activity.
